nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_koniec].text.t: Your husband lies by the wall, third row from the shrine.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_start].text.t: Your daughter said you live here.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_start_z].tex.t: I've seen your daughter. It's about the amulet.

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Jaga the widow stands by the fence with her hands folded over her belly, looking at you as if you were carrying a letter she's been afraid to read.

nodes.q9_koniec.text.t: Jaga falls silent, and then does something you don't expect: she smiles, thin as a thread. "Third row. He liked that corner, the sun looked in there of an afternoon. God repay you. Here, take what I have: a bit of meat to trade. I can't give more, because I haven't got it, but whoever brings good news doesn't leave empty-handed."

nodes.q9_start.text.t: Jaga blinks slowly. "My Ela? She came a few days ago with the amulet and cried the whole evening. My husband was a guard at the ruins, and he died when the Imperials closed the place. I don't know where they buried him. Jerzy the digger likely knows, but I haven't the nerve to ask. Will you ask for me?"

nodes.q9_start_z.text.t: Jaga presses her lips together till they vanish. "You kept it. So be it, it's a keepsake. I won't take it from you. But my man lies somewhere here in the ground, and I want to know where. Jerzy the digger ought to know. Will you ask for me?"
